How to track your AI visibility

Rank tracking shows your Google position. AI visibility shows whether assistants recommend you at all. Here is what to measure, how often, and which numbers are vanity.

What AI visibility actually measures

AI visibility is the measurement layer for GEO. Four numbers cover it:

  • Mentions: how many tracked AI answers name your brand. The baseline existence metric.
  • Share of voice: your slice of all mentions in your category versus competitors. The scoreboard metric.
  • Cited pages: which of your URLs appear inside answers. The asset metric, because it tells you what to make more of.
  • Trend: whether each of the above is rising or falling month over month. The only metric that proves your work is doing anything.

You can get the first one free in ten seconds with the AI visibility checker. The other three need a tracker that stores history, because single snapshots cannot show movement.

Why rank tracking doesn't cover this

Google and AI assistants pick sources differently. You can hold position 3 for "best crm for agencies" and still be absent from ChatGPT's answer for the same question, because the assistant assembled its shortlist from comparison articles and community threads rather than the ranking pages. The reverse also happens. Two scoreboards, two sets of levers, and a growing share of buyers reads only the second one.

The metrics that matter (and the vanity ones)

Matter:

  • Mentions per platform. ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews cite different sources; treat them as separate channels.
  • Share of voice versus named competitors. Five mentions means little if your category leader has two hundred.
  • Cited page concentration. When one page earns most citations, you have found a repeatable format. Build more of it.
  • Question coverage. The share of buyer questions in your category where you appear at all.

Vanity:

  • Impressions without questions. Volume numbers with no query context cannot be acted on.
  • One-time snapshots. A single check answers "am I mentioned", never "am I growing".
  • Global counts for local businesses. The data is market-specific; track the market you sell in.

Build a tracking routine that survives busy weeks

  1. Baseline once, properly. Run a full brand lookup across ChatGPT and AI Overviews for your domain and your three closest competitors. Save it.
  2. Review monthly, not daily. AI answers shift slowly between data refreshes. Daily checking adds noise and anxiety, not signal.
  3. Watch the delta questions. The report that matters lists questions where a competitor is mentioned and you are not. That list is your editorial calendar.
  4. Alert on drops. Disappearing from a category question you used to own is the AI equivalent of losing a page-one ranking; you want to know within days. Set an alert on mention movement.
  5. Tie every content ship to a number. Shipped a comparison page? Check whether the related question flipped to mentioning you within three weeks. Ship, measure, repeat.

Free check versus tracked report

The free checker answers the existence question, "does ChatGPT mention me", instantly and without an account. A tracked report inside AI brand visibility stores history, adds AI Overviews, competitor share of voice, every cited page, and alerts, so the trend line draws itself. Use the free check to recruit your team ("look, we're at zero"), use the tracker to run the project.

The scoreboard that changes decisions

The moment teams see share of voice, content debates change. Instead of arguing about topics by taste, the question becomes "which of these unanswered questions has the most volume and the weakest cited sources", and the roadmap writes itself. That is the real output of tracking: not a dashboard, a priority list.
